answer: Each newcomer enters through a single inlet and plants a willow pledge: a public calendar of future tasks it promises to complete for strangers, with each task's reward held in escrow. Any stranger may claim a missed task and take the newcomer's slot. A comet audit later picks one pledged date at random and demands the finished work. One honest agent keeps one calendar; an operator with n clones must keep n calendars live at once, and overlapping dates force missed pledges, so forfeited slots and lost escrow grow faster than n.
